lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a web app named App1 that sends requests to a multimodal chat model deployment in a Microsoft Foundry project.  
  
User messages can contain both text and images.  
  
Currently, App1 embeds the image URL as plain text within the message content, so the model cannot recognize it as an image.  
  
Traces show that the requests contain a single text message rather than a multimodal content array.  
  
You need to send the message as a structured array that includes both the text portion and the image reference, so that the model can process the image correctly.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Set the user message content array to include items that have type: text and type: image_url.
Encode the image to base64 and include the encoded data inside the content string of the user message.
Add the image URL to the request metadata section, so the model can resolve the processing issue automatically.
Place the image URL inside the System Message and set type to image_url so the model loads the image at initialization.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Foundry (Azure OpenAI) chat completion models that support vision expect the user message's 'content' field to be an array of content-part objects rather than a plain string when the message includes both text and images. Each element in the array must specify a 'type': one element with type 'text' containing the text field, and another with type 'image_url' containing an 'image_url' object with the image's URL (or base64 data URI). This structured format allows the model to distinguish text from image references and process the image correctly, as documented in Microsoft's guidance on using image and audio input in chat completions with Foundry Models.

**Learn more:** [How to use image and audio in chat completions with Azure AI Foundry Models - Azure AI Foundry | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/model-inference/how-to/use-chat-multi-modal) · [How to use vision-enabled chat models - Microsoft Foundry | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/gpt-with-vision)

You are developing a customer support web application called App1 in Microsoft Foundry that uses a GPT realtime model.  
  
App1 must support:  
  
- Live, low-latency voice conversations powered by Azure OpenAI  
- Streaming audio input from users, along with playback of audio responses  
  
You need to select a connection method that supports real-time audio streaming within the client application and achieves approximately 100 ms of latency.  
  
Which connection method should you choose?
questions.explanation:
WebRTC is purpose-built for peer-to-peer, real-time audio (and video) communication and is the connection method Microsoft recommends for client-side applications—such as browser-based or mobile apps—that use the Azure OpenAI GPT Realtime API to stream microphone audio to the model and play back generated speech with minimal delay, typically achieving round-trip latencies around 100 ms. WebSocket, while supported by the Realtime API, is intended for server-to-server integrations where strict low latency is not required, since it introduces higher end-to-end delay than WebRTC. SIP is intended for telephony/PSTN call integration rather than in-browser or in-app client streaming, and RTMP is not a supported protocol for the Realtime API at all.

**Learn more:** [Use the GPT Realtime API via WebRTC - Microsoft Foundry | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/realtime-audio-webrtc) · [Use the GPT Realtime API via WebSockets - Microsoft Foundry | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/realtime-audio-websockets)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Foundry project.  
  
You need to deploy a model from the model catalog to support a search solution for internal policy documents. The model must generate vector representations of the text in the documents and of user queries.  
  
Which type of model should you use?
questions.explanation:
An embedding model is designed to convert text (documents and queries) into numerical vector representations that capture semantic meaning. These vectors enable similarity-based search, such as vector search or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), by allowing the system to compare the vector of a user query against the vectors of indexed documents to find the most relevant matches. The Azure AI Foundry (Microsoft Foundry) model catalog includes embedding models such as text-embedding-ada-002 and other embedding models specifically for this purpose, distinct from LLMs or SLMs which are optimized for text generation rather than producing embeddings.

**Learn more:** [Embeddings - Azure OpenAI Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/concepts/understand-embeddings) · [Model catalog and collections in Azure AI Foundry portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/how-to/model-catalog-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Foundry project.  
  
You need to deploy a model from the model catalog to support real-time inference. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Use key-based authentication.  
- Support real-time REST API access.  
- Must NOT consume the vCPU quota of the virtual machines in the Azure subscription.  
  
Which type of deployment should you use?
questions.explanation:
Serverless API (Models-as-a-Service) deployments in Azure AI Foundry are hosted and billed on a pay-as-you-go basis by Microsoft rather than being provisioned onto dedicated VM instances in the customer's subscription, so they do not draw from the subscription's vCPU quota. They expose a real-time REST API endpoint and are authenticated using an API key (key-based authentication), satisfying all stated requirements. In contrast, standard (managed compute) and self-hosted container deployments provision dedicated VM instances that consume subscription vCPU quota, and batch deployments are designed for asynchronous/offline processing rather than real-time REST calls.

**Learn more:** [Deploy models as serverless API deployments - Azure AI Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/how-to/deploy-models-serverless) · [Overview: Deploy models, flows, and web apps with Azure AI Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/concepts/deployments-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Foundry project containing an agent that generates summaries from retrieved policy documents.  
  
You need to improve the completeness of the agent's responses. The solution must be implemented in the application code logic, and it must take effect before responses are returned to the caller.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add a retry evaluation before the responses are returned.
Decrease the value of the temperature parameter.
Increase the value of the presence_penalty parameter
Replace the model with a smaller deployment.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Foundry provides built-in response-quality evaluators (including a completeness/answer-completeness metric) that can be called from application code to assess a generated response before it is returned to the user. By adding a retry-evaluation step in the app logic—evaluating the draft response for completeness and triggering a retry (regeneration or additional retrieval) when it fails the threshold—the application enforces completeness at runtime, prior to returning the final response. This differs from adjusting model sampling parameters (temperature, presence_penalty) or swapping to a smaller model, none of which are code-level pre-return quality gates and none of which reliably guarantee response completeness.

**Learn more:** [Agent Evaluators for Generative AI - Microsoft Foundry | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/evaluation-evaluators/agent-evaluators) · [Evaluate your AI agents - Microsoft Foundry | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/observability/how-to/evaluate-agent)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You are planning to build an application that will use the Azure AI DALL-E model.  
  
You need to deploy the model.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: the Azure SDK for Python and PowerShell cmdlets.
the Azure SDK for JavaScript and Azure Machine Learning Studio.
Microsoft Foundry and the Azure Command Line Interface (CLI)
the Azure portal and Microsoft Graph API

questions.explanation:
Deploying an Azure OpenAI model such as DALL-E requires creating a model deployment inside an Azure OpenAI/Azure AI resource. Microsoft Foundry (the current portal experience for Azure AI/Azure OpenAI resources) is the primary interface for creating and deploying such models, and the Azure CLI (using the cognitiveservices extension, e.g., `az cognitiveservices account deployment create`) provides a supported command-line/automation method for creating those deployments. This combination is documented in Microsoft's official guidance on deploying models in Microsoft Foundry, whereas the other tool combinations listed (Azure ML Studio, Microsoft Graph API, or the Python/PowerShell SDK/cmdlet pairing) are not the supported mechanism for deploying Azure OpenAI's DALL-E model.

**Learn more:** [Deploy models using Azure CLI and Bicep - Microsoft Foundry | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/how-to/create-model-deployments) · [How to Use Image Generation Models from OpenAI - Microsoft Foundry | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/dall-e)

You are working on a custom named entity recognition (NER) project in Azure Language in Foundry Tools for support tickets. The project schema includes an entity type called ContactInfo.  
  
In the tagged training files, ContactInfo is applied to:  
  
- Phone numbers  
- Email addresses  
- Social media handles  
  
When you evaluate the model, you observe low precision for the ContactInfo entity, including false positives where nearby text is incorrectly extracted as ContactInfo.  
  
You need to improve the precision of the project.  
  
What should you do before retraining the model?

options.text: Lower the confidence threshold for ContactInfo.
Add more support tickets as training data and label more ContactInfo entities.
Replace ContactInfo by using Phone, Email, and SocialMedia entities. Relabel every matching span.

questions.explanation:
Azure's custom NER schema-design guidance states that you should avoid 'complex entities' — entity types that bundle together multiple distinct kinds of information with different surface patterns — because such entities are difficult for the model to pick out precisely from text, leading to boundary confusion and false positives. The documented remedy is to break the complex entity into multiple, more specific entity types so each has a narrower, more consistent pattern that requires fewer labels to learn accurately (the official example replaces a single 'Address' entity with 'Street Name,' 'PO Box,' 'City,' 'State,' and 'Zip'). In this project, ContactInfo mixes phone numbers, email addresses, and social media handles — three very different textual patterns — under one label, which is exactly the kind of complex/ambiguous entity design that causes low precision and nearby-text false positives. Replacing ContactInfo with separate Phone, Email, and SocialMedia entities and relabeling the corresponding spans in the training data addresses the root schema issue before retraining, whereas adjusting the confidence threshold, running auto-labeling, or simply adding more training data with the same flawed schema would not resolve the underlying ambiguity.

**Learn more:** [Preparing data and designing a schema for custom named entity recognition (NER) - Foundry Tools | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/language-service/custom-named-entity-recognition/how-to/design-schema) · [Custom Named Entity Recognition (NER) FAQ - Foundry Tools | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/language-service/custom-named-entity-recognition/faq)

You are creating a text-to-speech solution using Azure Speech in Foundry Tools that reads instructions aloud from a script contained in a text file.  
  
You notice that the solution frequently mispronounces technical terms.  
  
You need to stop these incorrect pronunciations from occurring. The solution must minimize development effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From Speech Studio, train a custom neural voice
Use Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) to specify phonemes.
Use Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) to apply say as rules.
Use Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) to adjust the prosody of the voice.
From Azure OpenAI use the Whisper model.

questions.explanation:
The SSML phoneme element allows you to specify the exact pronunciation of a word using a phonetic alphabet such as IPA or SAPI. This directly addresses mispronunciation of specific technical terms with minimal effort, since you only need to annotate the problematic words in the SSML markup rather than retrain a model. In contrast, say-as is meant for interpreting content types (like dates or numbers) rather than correcting phonetic pronunciation, prosody adjusts pitch/rate/volume rather than pronunciation, custom neural voice training requires substantial data collection and model training effort, and Whisper is a speech-to-text model, not applicable to a text-to-speech pronunciation issue.

**Learn more:** [Pronunciation with Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) - Speech service - Foundry Tools | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/speech-synthesis-markup-pronunciation) · [Phonetic sets for Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) - Microsoft Learn](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs/blob/main/articles/ai-services/speech-service/speech-ssml-phonetic-sets.md)

You are building a new sales system that will process user-generated video and text submitted through a public-facing website.  
  
You plan to notify users that their data has been processed by the sales system.  
  
Which responsible AI principle does this help satisfy?
questions.explanation:
Transparency is one of Microsoft's six Responsible AI principles (fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, and accountability). It requires that organizations be open about how data is collected, used, and stored, and that people understand how AI systems process their information and reach decisions. Notifying users that their data has been processed satisfies this requirement for transparency about data collection and use, helping build user trust and enabling informed choices about how their data is handled.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing a content management system.  
  
You need to ensure that the reading experience is optimized for users who have reduced comprehension and learning differences, such as dyslexia. The solution must minimize development effort.  
  
Which Azure service should you include in the solution?

options.text: Azure Document Intelligence in Foundry Tools

questions.explanation:
Azure AI Immersive Reader is specifically designed to improve reading comprehension for people with learning differences such as dyslexia, as well as for new readers and language learners. It provides built-in, proven accessibility features—text-to-speech read-aloud, syllabification, parts-of-speech highlighting, line focus, adjustable spacing/fonts, and a picture dictionary—through a ready-to-use client library and UI, which can be embedded into an application with minimal custom development. This distinguishes it from Document Intelligence (document data extraction), Language (general NLP tasks like sentiment/key phrase analysis), and Translator (language translation), none of which target reading comprehension accessibility.

**Learn more:** [What is Azure AI Immersive Reader? - Azure AI services | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/immersive-reader/overview) · [Azure AI Immersive Reader | Microsoft Azure](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/ai-services/ai-immersive-reader)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains an Azure App Service app named App1.  
  
You provision a Microsoft Foundry Service resource named CSAccount1.  
  
You need to configure App1 to access CSAccount1, using a solution that minimizes administrative effort.  
  
What should you use to configure App1?

options.text: the endpoint URI and subscription key
the endpoint URI and an OAuth token
the endpoint URI and a shared access signature (SAS) token
a system assigned managed identity and an X.509 certificate

questions.explanation:
A system-assigned managed identity provides App1 with an automatically created and managed identity in Microsoft Entra ID. Behind the scenes, Azure issues and automatically rotates an X.509 certificate as the credential for this identity, so no keys, tokens, or secrets need to be manually created, stored, or rotated by an administrator. After enabling the managed identity, you simply assign App1's identity an appropriate RBAC role (such as Cognitive Services User) on CSAccount1, and the app authenticates using Microsoft Entra ID tokens obtained transparently through this managed credential. This keyless approach requires the least ongoing administrative effort compared to manually managing a subscription key, OAuth token, or SAS token.

**Learn more:** [Managed identities for Azure resources - overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/overview) · [How to use managed identities for App Service and Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-managed-identity)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an application that will use Azure AI Search for internal documents.  
  
You need to implement document-level filtering for Azure AI Search.  
  
Which three actions should you include in the solution? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
(Choose three.)

options.text: Add allowed groups to each index entry
Send access tokens from Microsoft Entra ID, with the search request.
Retrieve the group memberships of the user
Supply the groups as a filter for the search requests

questions.explanation:
Azure AI Search does not provide built-in row-level or document-level security, so filtering must be implemented manually using the security filter pattern documented by Microsoft. This pattern requires: adding a filterable field to each index document that lists the group IDs (or user IDs) allowed to view that document; retrieving the group memberships of the requesting user (e.g., via Microsoft Graph or a token claim) at query time; and supplying those group IDs as an OData filter expression on the search request (such as group_ids/any(g:search.in(g, 'group_id1,group_id2'))) so that only documents matching the user's group memberships are returned in the results.

**Learn more:** [Security filters for trimming results - Azure AI Search](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-security-trimming-for-azure-search) · [Security trimming example using Microsoft Entra ID - Azure AI Search](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-security-trimming-for-azure-search-with-aad)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure AI Search indexer that ingests PDF policy manuals.  
  
Client applications must display page-level citations that include bounding polygons for both text and images.  
  
You need to add a single built-in multimodal content extraction skill to the Azure AI Search skillset. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Provide text and image location metadata.  
- Extract tables that span multiple pages.  
  
What should you add?
questions.explanation:
The Document Layout skill (Microsoft.Skills.Util.DocumentIntelligenceLayoutSkill) calls the Azure Document Intelligence layout model to analyze document structure. When its extractionOptions parameter includes "images" and "locationMetadata", the skill's outputs (text_sections and normalized_images) each include a locationMetadata object containing pageNumber and boundingPolygons, giving precise page-level citation data for both text and images. Because it relies on the Document Intelligence layout model, it also detects and preserves table structure, including tables that span multiple pages, as part of its structural analysis. This makes it the single built-in skill that satisfies both the text/image location metadata requirement and the multi-page table extraction requirement, unlike Document Extraction (no location metadata), GenAI Prompt (generative enrichment, not structural extraction), or Azure Content Understanding (a separate content analysis service/skill not aligned with this classic layout-based bounding polygon output).

**Learn more:** [Document Layout Skill - Azure AI Search | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/cognitive-search-skill-document-intelligence-layout) · [Tutorial: Multimodal Chunking and Embedding with the Document Layout Skill - Azure AI Search | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/tutorial-document-layout-multimodal-embeddings)
